How has Tom Vek’s sound changed since his early records?

A reviewer described the debut We Have Sound as lo-fi bedroom rock with thick, dry drums, jangly angular guitars and a DIY feel. 2 The same reviewer heard a sign in the B-side 'Things Are Here To Stay' that Tom Vek would move from rock toward something more electronic on later albums. 2 The supplied sources don't describe his later albums' sound directly, so how far that shift went isn't covered here. 2

How has Tom Vek’s sound changed since his early records?

Tom Vek described his early "sound" as starting from a tape recording of drums that he looped up in the studio with producer Tom Rixton to build a song around. 1 He described his early-2000s b-side material as scuzzy electro instrumentals. 2 The supplied sources don't directly compare his early albums with his later records in sonic terms; they mostly describe his process and gear. 1

What should I listen for to hear that change?

On New Symbols, a 2020 review heard loud, dense songs with driving synth progressions, winding guitars, rolling percussion and swirling synths, sometimes pushing the vocals into second place. 3 These sources are reviews and an interview, not a direct side-by-side comparison, so the contrast above is drawn from separate descriptions of each album. 3

Navigator-v2 independent review

Finding: The follow-up finds and uses New Symbols, giving concrete later-album listening cues, but filtering leaves an orphaned reference to “the contrast above.”

Usefulness Assessment: Driving synth progressions, winding guitars, rolling percussion and vocals sometimes pushed back give a listener something useful to hear. The answer does not present a coherent within-answer comparison after its early and middle-period sentences are removed.

Followup Assessment: The planner resolves the actual F04 antecedent to We Have Sound versus later albums without forcing a source URL. The later-album details advance that thread; the initial answer’s limitations are not counted again as a separate missing antecedent.

Run methods, code pins, and limits

The original F04 card comes from the earlier fan-experience cohort. The fixed-v1 and navigator-v2 runs use the same frozen saved-corpus export: their corpus hashes match. The original run’s corpus export is shown separately in its provenance pin because it is a different historical snapshot. No full corpus text is embedded.

The navigator-v2 result uses the actual artist-question flow and the app’s saved-original navigator over the frozen corpus. It adds no external lookup or collection. Authentication, persistence, and durable job lifecycle remain harness seams; this does not establish deployed authentication, jobs, or production latency. F04 is a targeted known-case diagnostic. N01 is a newly authored follow-up, not a paired before/after case. Neither is held out or representative.

The previous fixed-v1 review describes an answer that still missed the requested across-record sonic comparison. The new result should be judged only from its saved answer and a separately locked review. This selective F04/N01 report does not replace the full 17-case confirmation.
